summary.text: Momentum is a measure of motion equal to an object's mass times its velocity, counted in kilogram metres per second.
Because it has a direction as well as a size, it can be used to predict where objects head and how fast they move after they collide.
In a closed system with no outside forces the total momentum never changes, and the net force on a body equals how quickly its momentum changes.

facts.label: Link to force
facts.value: Net force equals the rate of change of momentum

facts.label: Conserved when
facts.value: No outside forces act on a closed system

items.prompt: Two planes of equal mass fly at 50 m/s, one north and one south. How do their momenta compare?

options.label: Identical, since mass and speed match
The southbound one is larger
Equal in size but pointing opposite ways
Both are zero because they cancel

items.explain: Momentum is a vector, so equal size with opposite direction is not the same momentum.

items.prompt: A 1 kg model plane speeds from rest to 6 m/s north in 2 s. What net force does that take?

options.label: 3 newtons north
6 newtons north
12 newtons north
1 newton north

items.explain: The momentum changes by 6 kg⋅m/s over 2 s, which is 3 per second, and that rate equals the net force in newtons.

items.prompt: Several particles move together as one system. Their total mass is m, and their center of mass moves at velocity v_cm. What is the system's momentum?

options.label: The mass of the heaviest particle times v_cm
Zero, because the particles' motions cancel out
The average particle mass times v_cm
p = mv_cm

items.explain: The momentum of the system is the total mass times the velocity of its center of mass: p = mv_cm.

items.prompt: Two skaters at rest on frictionless ice shove each other apart, with nothing else pushing them. What happens to their total momentum?

options.label: It grows because they now move
It stays the same as before the shove
It is zero only while they touch
It turns into kinetic energy

items.explain: With no outside forces the total momentum does not change, including when objects are pushed apart.

items.prompt: A 2 kg cart rolls at 3 m/s. What is its momentum in SI units?

options.label: 5 kg⋅m/s
1.5 kg⋅m/s
6 kg⋅m/s
9 kg⋅m/s

items.explain: Momentum is mass times velocity: 2 times 3 is 6 kg⋅m/s.

items.prompt: Two carts on a track push against each other, and cart 1's momentum begins to grow. What happens to cart 2's momentum?

options.label: It changes at the same rate, in the opposite direction
It changes at the same rate, in the same direction
It stays fixed because only one cart is pushed
It changes faster because the forces add together

items.explain: The forces between the two are equal in size and opposite in direction, so dp₁/dt = −dp₂/dt.
